deliverable: Layer 2: GP/random-walk latent-force MFE estimate + damping-vs-residual decomposition
method: per-mode modal SDOF + random-walk latent force; RTS Kalman SMOOTHER (linear-Gaussian FILTER, NOT NUTS)
sampler_label: exact linear-Gaussian RTS smoother; process/measurement noise fixed/empirical (NOT a posterior)
decomposition: latent modal force g(t) projected on velocity v: velocity-explained variance = viscous DAMPING share, residual = non-viscous/nonlinear MFE; Delta_zeta = -<g,v>/<v,v>/(2*w0)
observability: one latent force PER MODE (low-dim modal basis, not per-DOF); band-pass isolates the mode so the chosen sensors observe it; close-mode clusters (234/244/254 etc.) mix and inflate residual
caveat: the latent-force variance SPLIT (damping_fraction vs residual_fraction) is contaminated by smoother process noise and by close-mode beating in clusters, so it is NOT used as the headline; the robust, q_g-stable products are (i) the velocity-projection zeta_true and (ii) the nonlinearity diagnostics.
verdict: ROBUST: the latent-force smoother's velocity-projection recovers zeta_true ~0.58% (vs FEM nominal 1.0% -> FEM is OVER-damped), and it CROSS-CHECKS the independent log-decrement zeta per trace (corr ~0.82) and the Layer-1 NUTS posterior -> the latent MFE force is dominantly a viscous DAMPING correction (the parsimonious 'FEM has the wrong zeta'). The genuine NON-VISCOUS residual shows NO amplitude dependence (residual-vs-q^2 corr ~0.03) and near-exponential decay (early/late-decay zeta ratio ~1.08) -> little evidence of strong missing NONLINEAR physics. So the model-form error here is MOSTLY wrong DAMPING (parsimonious), not missing physics. (The raw variance split is q_g/beating-contaminated; see caveat.)
